note: Track runs (voice-runs), step 1: Do to Sol and back, one note per beat on a staff, then the book's run in eighths and in sixteenths. missing: a run-singer prop that caps the top note or the number of keys (its last pass always reaches the top of the voice's range, too high for a beginner, so the text says where to stop).

exercise.title: Do to Sol and back, as a run
exercise.why: A run is steps you already sing, sung faster, so you set the five notes in place slowly first and then keep the same notes while the beat packs in two and then four of them.

cells.text:
Press Start exercise below: the metronome and the mic start together, and your pitch shows as a line on the staff. Sing from the low {{1}} up to {{5}} and back down, one note per beat. Sing them on the note names.
Practice until each note lands on its click without a slide.

Press Play below to hear the run: two chords set the key, and the mic starts with them. The run goes from Do up to Sol and back, two notes per beat. Each pass starts a semitone higher. Sing along on "ah", and move to "oo" as the passes climb.
If the notes smear into each other, sing one pass on "la", then go back to "ah".
_Don't reach for high notes: stop singing at the pass where the run stops feeling easy, and listen to the rest._

Press Play below to hear the run: two chords set the key, and the mic starts with them. Now the run goes from Do up to Sol and back twice in each pass, four notes per beat. Each pass starts a semitone higher. Sing along lightly on "ah", and move to "oo" as the passes climb.
If the notes come out late, sing only the first note of each beat for one pass, then put the others back in.
